title: The Surprising Power of Atomic Habits
coreMove: Treat invisible progress as banked evidence and keep improving the system while results lag.
sourcePressure: Tiny improvements compound, systems govern trajectory, and results often lag behind habit structure.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Thinking tiny habits are motivational slogans or that small effort deserves immediate visible payoff.

hook: starting with a definition of 1 percent better
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: a velodrome mechanic logging tiny bearing adjustments for a junior cycling squad
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach whose riders are still losing by a wheel length
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether he scraps marginal gains before race-day speed appears
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he overlays the torque logs with lap times and sees the tenth-second gains arrive only after eight quiet weeks
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a spreadsheet of tire-pressure notes beside a stripped hub

exampleSpecs.domain: a sourdough bakery shaving seconds from the morning scoring line
exampleSpecs.audience: a baker fighting a 5 a.m. production bottleneck
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether tiny prep changes prevent the Saturday queue from backing out the door
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she totals eight seconds saved per loaf across ninety loaves and keeps the new blade layout another month
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a razor blade set beside flour-dusted proofing baskets

exampleSpecs.domain: a municipal water lab calibrating a sensor one decimal point at a time
exampleSpecs.audience: a technician under pressure to replace equipment
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether small calibration records prevent a false contamination alarm
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he points to six minor drift corrections and chooses another calibration cycle instead of buying a new unit
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a chlorine sensor blinking beside a laminated log

exampleSpecs.domain: a novice cellist raising bow speed by two metronome clicks per practice
exampleSpecs.audience: an adult beginner embarrassed by slow progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she quits before tone quality changes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the teacher plays week-one and week-nine recordings back to back so the hidden gains become audible
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a phone recorder glowing on a black music stand

exampleSpecs.domain: a credit-union borrower sending tiny extra payments against principal
exampleSpecs.audience: a teller coaching a member who feels the balance is frozen
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the member stops autopay because the statement looks unchanged
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the teller circles the month where interest drops below principal and asks the member to protect the boring stretch
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a loan statement folded under a plastic desk shield

exampleSpecs.domain: a soil-restoration crew measuring organic matter after cover-crop cycles
exampleSpecs.audience: a farm manager tempted to abandon the field trial
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether invisible soil gains are respected before yield rises
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the crew compares soil tests from three seasons and names the threshold that was not visible from the road
exampleSpecs.firstImage: dark soil crumbling through a sieve at the edge of a test plot

skillTargets: separate lagging outcomes from leading habit evidence
choose system repairs over goal resets
detect when small gains are being dismissed too early

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one habit with no visible payoff yet. Name one leading measure you can bank today, such as one logged rep, one setup action, or one tiny reduction in friction.
